literature.comparison_level: PRACTICAL SCENARIO, not a literature replication. Asks the investor-relevant question: over a long, multi-regime horizon (2011-2024), does the transformer pipeline (model mu + shared/sample Sigma) pay off against the plain historical pipeline (sample-mean mu + sample Sigma) and against a passive S&P 500 buy-and-hold? Diversified large-cap universe, monthly rebalancing with annual retraining, K=20 with a 10% per-name cap. Universe is filtered to full-history survivors (survivorship bias inflates absolute returns for ALL strategies equally; the transformer-vs-historical comparison is relative and largely unaffected, but the index gap should be read as a lower bound).

reference_values.note: No external anchor; headline metrics are long-term terminal wealth, CAGR, annualized Sharpe and maximum drawdown, plus the equity curve vs SPY.

notes: FAIRNESS/UNITS: horizon scaling (automatic) scales historical mu AND Sigma by H=21 so they match the transformers' raw 21-day mu. Before this fix TFT/PatchTST mu had 69x/92x the cross-sectional dispersion of the historical mu while facing a 1-DAY Sigma, so the risk term was numerically irrelevant and they were effectively running max-return top-K selection inside the w_max box rather than mean-variance. Scaling both moments is a no-op for the Historical/MASTER solutions (H factors out of the objective).

FAIRNESS/CADENCE: moment_refit=match_models re-estimates historical mu/Sigma on exactly the cutoff the models were last refit on (model_refit=annual), instead of 'expanding' which refreshed the baseline every MONTH while the models refit once a YEAR. On the Leow All-Weather protocol that same asymmetry was worth 4.4 Sharpe points to the baseline.

FAIRNESS/RISK-MATCHING: P grid widened from a single point to 11 so `python benchmark/run.py risk-matched --dir <output_dir>` can report each model at matched REALIZED volatility. Adds ~1.1h of solver time, no extra training.

SEEDS: deliberately single-seed (42). With 168 monthly decisions the sampling noise that made the 13-decision Leow protocol a seed lottery is far better averaged; a 5-seed ensemble would multiply a 14-year/61-asset/3-model run by 5 for little gain.
